They might be key workers who have worked all the way through the Covid-19 pandemic without a proper break in the past year. They might have been home-schooling and juggling work with childcare. One Revolution will have a positive impact on the community by: 3 Empowering disadvantaged youth with access to cycling and skills training, giving them opportunities they might not otherwise have. 3 Reducing the risk of negative social behaviors by providing a structured and supportive environment where participants can focus on personal and athletic development. 3 Fostering social inclusion by creating a responsible peer group and promoting teamwork and community engagement among participants. 3 Contributing to the overall well-being of the community by developing healthier, more confident, and engaged young people who are better equipped to contribute positively to society.

Expand and improve our cycling and sports programs for disadvantaged youth. Provide additional training, resources, and equipment for participants. Support pathways to employment through fully funded skills training and educational opportunities. Should the company wish to donate or fundraise for other charitable causes, this will only be done with the consent of the CIC Regulator.

name: TWALK CIC
description: TWALK CIC is dedicated to supporting business professionals, entrepreneurs, and individuals working in isolation within the United Kingdom. Our services will primarily focus on County Durham and North Yorkshire with plans to expand to neighbouring areas as the community grows.  The region is home to a diverse group of professionals from various industries, including tech, finance, creative arts, and consultancy. Many of these individuals either work remotely, run their own businesses, or are part of small teams, leading to feelings of professional isolation and a lack of peer support. This is particularly true in rural and semi-urban areas surrounding County Durham and North Yorkshire, where opportunities for networking and professional engagement can be limited.  TWALK CIC addresses these challenges by offering walk-and-talk therapy and consultancy sessions in natural, outdoor settings. This approach not only promotes mental well-being but also fosters meaningful connections among participants. By leveraging the region's beautiful landscapes, such as the local Parks such as South Park in Darlington, the Yorkshire Dales, North York Moors, and Lake District we create an environment that encourages open conversations and the sharing of ideas.  Our services are designed to benefit:  1. Entrepreneurs and Small Business Owners: Those managing businesses on their own or with small teams who lack regular peer interaction.  2. Remote Workers and Freelancers: Individuals who work from home and miss the social and professional engagement of a traditional office setting.  3. Professionals Experiencing Burnout or Stress: Those in high-pressure roles seeking a healthier work-life balance and mental health support.  4. People New to the Area: Individuals who have recently moved to County Durham and North Yorkshire and are looking for ways to integrate into the professional community.  5. Individuals who are feeling Isolated: We aim to help combat loneliness for those people who live alone.  Through TWALK CIC, we aim to build a supportive network that reduces isolation, enhances professional development, and improves overall well-being. By combining the therapeutic benefits of nature with professional consultancy, we create a unique space where business people can thrive both personally and professionally.

name: HUSTLE HIVE CIC
description:
The company's activities will provide benefit to young people at risk of exclusion, home-educated children, people with disabilities and special educational needs, unemployed or underemployed adults, and aspiring entrepreneurs within the local and surrounding communities. This includes individuals who face barriers to mainstream education or employment and those seeking to gain practical skills, qualifications, and support to start their own businesses.  The company aims to serve a broad community across all ages, with a particular focus on those who are underserved, disengaged, or looking to re-engage through creative, outdoor, digital, and enterprise-based learning opportunities.

If the company makes any surplus, it will be reinvested into expanding community access to education, skills training, and entrepreneurship support. This includes subsidising places for disadvantaged learners, maintaining and upgrading equipment such as 3D printers, laser cutters, and media tools, investing in outdoor education equipment and extending the availability of alternative provision for excluded students. Surplus may also be used to develop new workshops, fund outreach activities, support community events, or provide micro-grants and resources for individuals developing business ideas through the hub. Where surplus is donated or fundraised for external charities, this will be done with the consent of the CIC Regulator.

description: The charity's objects (Objects) are specifically restricted to the following:  to relieve need, suffering and distress amongst veterans or those leaving the armed forces, in such ways as the trustees shall think fit, particularly but not exclusively by providing work placements to wounded, injured and sick veterans or those leaving the armed forces who have suffered the effects of war and have found the transition from military to civilian life difficult as a means to preserve and protect their physical and mental health, support their resettlement, rehabilitation, if needed and their retraining to help them obtain employment.
